Lancelot. Sir Lancelot du Lac stands as the greatest knight of the Round Table, unmatched in courage and martial prowess, yet his love for Queen Guinevere becomes the tragic flaw that brings down the kingdom he served so faithfully. His story exemplifies the medieval conflict between chivalric duty and human desire.

He was raised by the Lady of the Lake in the magical realm of Lac, hence his epithet "du Lac." Lancelot was widely considered the strongest and most skilled warrior of Arthur's knights, renowned for quests and tournaments. He fathered Galahad with Elaine, a union orchestrated through deception, producing the knight destined to achieve the Holy Grail.

Lancelot carried on a passionate, ultimately public affair with Queen Guinevere, violating his oath to Arthur. His rescue of Guinevere from execution by burning sparked civil war among the Round Table knights. He was driven into exile after Camelot's collapse; some traditions claim he became a hermit or monk in his final years. He represents the paradox of the perfect knight destroyed not by weakness but by the nobility of his own heart.

His connections bind him to tragedy: King Arthur, the king he served and betrayed; Guinevere, the queen he loved forbidden; Galahad, his son, the purest knight who alone could achieve the Holy Grail; and the Round Table, the fellowship his passion fractured.
